name: Barbell Bench Press
why: Supine, and the heaviest horizontal press available. Lying flat is avoided after the first trimester.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
why: Supine press; the narrow grip concentrates load at the elbow.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
why: Supine. Dumbbells allow a deeper stretch at the bottom than a bar.

name: Machine Bench Press
why: Supine and fixed-path; the path is what a restricted shoulder cannot adjust.

name: Standing Cable Wood Chop
why: Rotation under load, though driven from the hips rather than the lumbar spine.

name: Calf Raises - With Bands
why: Lightest ankle loading available.

name: Seated Calf Raise
why: Bent knee moves the work to the soleus; ankle range is the same.

name: Standing Calf Raise
why: Full ankle range under bodyweight.

name: Band Chest Press
why: Upright and light. The mildest press in the library and the one a pregnant practitioner can keep.

name: Chest Dip
why: Deep shoulder extension under bodyweight — the position most associated with anterior shoulder strain.

name: Decline Push-Up
why: Head-below-heart position with the shoulder near end range.

name: Incline Push-Up
why: The most prenatal-friendly press: upright, self-limiting, no supine position.

name: Knee Push-Up
why: As the push-up, with less load through the wrist and shoulder.

name: Push-Up
why: Loaded wrist extension. Trunk stays off the floor, so it is workable in pregnancy for as long as the belly allows.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
why: The longest anti-extension lever there is, with the shoulders holding the position.

name: Bird Dog
why: Quadruped, low load, spine neutral. Safe for essentially everyone, including prenatally.

name: Cable Crunch
why: Weighted spinal flexion — the highest-load flexion movement in the library.

name: Cat-Cow
why: Unloaded spinal movement through a self-selected range. Suitable prenatally.

name: Child's Pose
why: Deep knee flexion in the kneeling position; the spine is unloaded.

name: Crunches
why: Repeated loaded spinal flexion. Abdominal separation makes this unsuitable prenatally.

name: Dead Bug
why: Supine. One of the better trunk drills for a sensitive back, since the range is set by the back staying flat.

name: Exercise Ball Crunch
why: As the crunch, through a longer range.

name: Exercise Ball Pull-In
why: Plank on an unstable base; the shoulders support throughout.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
why: Hanging loads the shoulder throughout; the pelvis must tilt before the legs move.

name: Hollow Body Hold
why: Supine with a long lever; the low back lifts the moment the trunk gives.

name: Leg Raise on Parallel Bars
why: Supported on the forearms, so less shoulder load than hanging.

name: Lying Leg Raise
why: Supine with a long lever; the low back arches as soon as the abdominals are outmatched.

name: Plank
why: The trunk resists extension against gravity — a demand that rises sharply as the abdomen loads.

name: Russian Twist
why: Loaded rotation of a flexed spine — the position discs tolerate least.

name: Side Plank
why: The supporting shoulder carries the bodyweight.

name: Band Biceps Curl
why: Tension is lowest at full extension, where the elbow is most exposed.

name: Barbell Curl
why: Fixed supinated grip gives the elbow and wrist no room to adjust.

name: Cable Curl
why: Constant tension holds the elbow under load through the whole range.

name: Concentration Curls
why: Braced arm removes the escape route the standing versions allow.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
why: Free rotation lets the wrist and elbow find a comfortable path.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
why: The angled bar eases the wrist; the elbow load is unchanged.

name: Self-Resisted Biceps Curl
why: The practitioner sets the resistance, so it cannot exceed what they tolerate.

name: Towel Biceps Curl
why: As above — self-limiting by construction.

name: Barbell Deadlift
why: The heaviest axial pull available, with a brace held against a maximal effort.

name: Rack Pull
why: Heaviest axial load in the library. Breath-holding against a maximal pull is the mechanism.

name: Sumo Deadlift
why: As the conventional pull, with the wide stance loading the hip in abduction.

name: Dip Machine
why: Same shoulder position as a dip, with the load chosen rather than fixed.

name: External Rotation
why: Rotator-cuff rehab loading. Deliberately untagged: withholding it from a shoulder problem removes the treatment.

name: Face Pull
why: External rotation with abduction — the movement most often prescribed FOR a shoulder, not against it.

name: Farmer's Walk
why: Load hangs from the shoulder girdle through the neck; the spine itself stays neutral and braced.

name: Barbell Floor Press
why: Supine, so not prenatal — but the floor caps the range, which is why it carries no shoulder restriction: it is the press a restricted shoulder keeps.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
why: As above. Deliberately untagged for the shoulder so that someone with a shoulder problem is left with a pressing option.

name: Cable Crossover
why: Standing, so no supine restriction, but the same end-range shoulder position as a fly.

name: Dumbbell Flyes
why: Supine, and takes the shoulder to end-range horizontal abduction under load.

name: Pec Deck
why: Seated and fixed-path at end-range shoulder abduction.

name: Front Dumbbell Raise
why: Flexion to shoulder height with a long lever.

name: Front Barbell Squat
why: As the back squat, plus a rack position the shoulder and wrist must hold.

name: Goblet Squat
why: The chest-held weight keeps the torso upright and the load light. The squat that survives most restrictions.

name: Back Extension
why: Repeated lumbar extension. Prone position rules it out prenatally.

name: Good Morning
why: Bar on the back through a hinge — the longest lever against the spine of anything here.

name: Hack Squat
why: Fixed path holds the knee in one line whether or not that is the practitioner's line.

name: Cable Hammer Curl
why: Neutral grip with constant tension; the kindest loaded curl.

name: Hammer Curls
why: Neutral grip is the most forgiving curl for the elbow and wrist.

name: Adductor
why: End-range hip abduction; the load is the weight of the legs.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
why: Spine stays neutral and supported, so the disc restriction is dropped; the low back still resists extension at the top.

name: Glute Bridge
why: Supine, which rules it out after the first trimester. Otherwise among the gentlest hip movements.

name: Glute Bridge March
why: Supine bridge held while the trunk resists tilt.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
why: Supine, and the single-leg version asks the low back to resist rotation.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
why: Inclined rather than flat, but still a reclined position under a loaded bar.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
why: Reclined, and the incline shifts load onto the front of the shoulder.

name: Band Lateral Raise
why: Lightest abduction available; band tension is least where the arc is most sensitive.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
why: As the dumbbell version, with tension held at the bottom.

name: Side Lateral Raise
why: Abduction to shoulder height. Light, but directly through the painful arc.

name: Lying Leg Curls
why: Prone position rules it out prenatally; hamstring loading at the knee otherwise.

name: Seated Leg Curl
why: Seated and supported, so it keeps the hamstring work without the prone position.

name: 90/90 Hamstring
why: Passive stretch against a wall, range self-selected.

name: Band Pull-Through
why: Hinge pattern with the load pulling backwards rather than down — the least spinal compression of any hinge.

name: Leg Extensions
why: Open-chain knee extension puts shear through the joint that closed-chain work does not.

name: Lying Prone Quadriceps
why: End-range knee flexion, performed lying face down.

name: Seated Glute
why: Passive hip external rotation with a forward hinge.

name: Standing Hip Circles
why: Unloaded joint preparation through the hip's own range.

name: Leg Press
why: Deep knee flexion under heavy load; the low back rounds off the pad at depth.

name: Barbell Lunge
why: Loaded single-leg work with a bar on the back — balance fails before the muscles do.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
why: Deep single-leg flexion with the rear foot elevated; a demanding position for the front knee.

name: Dumbbell Lunges
why: Single-leg knee flexion under load; the dumbbells can be dropped, which the bar cannot.

name: Reverse Lunge
why: Stepping back rather than forward keeps the front shin vertical and is markedly kinder to the knee.

name: Split Squat
why: Both feet planted, so the balance demand is low and the knee path is stable.

name: Arm Circles
why: Unloaded joint preparation.

name: Arnold Dumbbell Press
why: Adds internal-to-external rotation under load, through the arc the cuff is most exposed in.

name: Band Overhead Press
why: Overhead, but band tension is lowest at the bottom and the load is small.

name: Band Pull Apart
why: Scapular retraction against light resistance. Safe for essentially everyone.

name: Barbell Shoulder Press
why: Overhead pressing with a bar; the bracing required raises intrathoracic pressure.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
why: Overhead, but seated and independently loaded so the arms find their own path.

name: Hands-Elevated Pike Push-Up
why: Less overhead load and less inversion than the floor version.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
why: Supported and fixed-path; suitable when balance rather than the shoulder is the limit.

name: Pike Push-Up
why: Bodyweight overhead press with the head below the heart.

name: Pike Push-Up - Feet Elevated
why: Near-vertical loading with the head well below the heart.

name: Plank Shoulder Tap
why: Loaded wrist extension in a plank; the plank position is unavailable as the abdomen loads.

name: Prone T-Raise
why: Light posterior shoulder work, performed face down.

name: Prone Y-Raise
why: As the T-raise, with more shoulder flexion.

name: Wall Handstand Hold
why: Full inversion under bodyweight; blood pressure and wrist load are both at their limit.

name: Wall Slide
why: Scapular rehab drill against a wall. The derived rule withheld it from shoulder problems, which is backwards.

name: Pallof Press
why: Anti-rotation: the trunk resists movement rather than producing it. Safe prenatally and with most back restrictions.

name: Preacher Curl
why: Loads the elbow at full extension, where the joint is least protected.

name: Standing Dumbbell Reverse Curl
why: Pronated grip loads the lateral elbow — the tennis-elbow mechanism.

name: Band Lat Pulldown
why: Overhead, but band tension is lowest at the top where the shoulder is most vulnerable.

name: V-Bar Pulldown
why: Neutral close grip is the kindest overhead pull; keeps `shoulder_injury` but not the cuff tag.

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
why: Overhead start position. Seated and supported, so no prenatal restriction.

name: Push Press
why: Explosive overhead drive with an axial load and a hard brace.

name: Band Triceps Pushdown
why: Lightest elbow extension available.

name: One-Arm Cable Pushdown
why: As the pushdown, one side at a time.

name: Triceps Pushdown
why: Standing and self-limiting, but the elbow is the working joint.

name: Bent Over Rear Delt Raise
why: Posterior shoulder work, which is generally protective. Hinged position rules it out prenatally.

name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
why: Standing and upright, so it keeps the posterior work without the hinge.

name: Reverse Flyes
why: As the rear delt raise.

name: Banded Romanian Deadlift
why: Lightest hinge in the library; tension is lowest at the bottom where the spine is most flexed.

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
why: Sustained loaded hinge; the hamstrings run out before the spine does, which is where it goes wrong.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
why: Same hinge, lighter load, dumbbells tracking closer to the body.

name: Band Row
why: Upright, light, and fully self-limiting.

name: Bent Over Barbell Row
why: Sustained loaded spinal flexion hold; the hinge position is also unavailable as the abdomen grows.

name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row
why: Unsupported hinge under load.

name: Chest Supported Dumbbell Row
why: The bench removes the spinal load entirely. This is the row that survives a back restriction.

name: Chin-Up
why: As the pull-up, with the supinated grip adding elbow load.

name: Doorway Row
why: Self-limiting and light — the resistance is your own lean.

name: Inverted Row
why: Bodyweight, spine neutral and supported by the feet. Among the safest pulls in the library.

name: Inverted Row - Underhand Grip
why: As the inverted row; the supinated grip loads the elbow.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
why: The bench takes most of the spinal load, so the disc restriction is dropped; still a hinged position.

name: Prone Swimmer
why: Light, but performed face down.

name: Pull-Up
why: Full overhead hang loads the shoulder at end range; hanging is also avoided as the abdomen loads.

name: Renegade Row
why: A plank under a rowing load; the trunk and the supporting shoulder both work hard.

name: Rowing Machine
why: Repeated loaded hinge at high cadence, where form fails as fatigue arrives.

name: Seated Cable Row
why: Seated and supported; the low back still works to hold the torso upright.

name: Superman Hold
why: Sustained lumbar extension, performed lying face down.

name: T-Bar Row
why: Same hinged position as a barbell row.

name: Wall Angel Row
why: Postural drill against a wall. Suitable for almost everyone, including prenatally.

name: Barbell Shrug
why: Heavy load hanging from the shoulder girdle, transmitted through the neck.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
why: As the barbell shrug.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
why: Loaded lateral flexion of the lumbar spine.

name: EZ-Bar Skullcrusher
why: As above, with the angled bar easing the wrist only.

name: Lying Triceps Press
why: Supine, and loads the elbow at end-range flexion.

name: Banded Squat
why: Band tension is highest standing and lowest at depth, which is the opposite of where the knee is loaded.

name: Barbell Squat
why: Axial load through the spine with a hard brace; the knee is at end-range flexion under that load.

name: Bodyweight Squat
why: No external load; depth is self-selected.

name: Box Squat to a Chair
why: The chair sets the depth, so the knee never passes into an unmanaged range.

name: Wall Sit
why: Sustained isometric knee flexion; the position is fixed and the load is bodyweight.

name: Barbell Step Ups
why: As above with an axial load and a balance demand on top.

name: Dumbbell Step Ups
why: Loaded single-leg knee extension; box height decides how much.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
why: Long-lever shoulder extension; the straight arm is what makes it a shoulder movement.

name: Suitcase Carry
why: One-sided load the trunk resists laterally.

name: Kettlebell Swing
why: Ballistic hinge; the spine decelerates the bell at the bottom of every rep.

name: Bench Dips
why: Internally rotated shoulder behind the torso — a poor position under load.

name: Bodyweight Triceps Extension
why: Self-limiting, but the elbow is the only joint working.

name: Close-Grip Push-Up
why: Loaded wrist extension with the elbows tracking close.

name: Diamond Push-Up
why: The narrowest hand position puts the wrist at its end range.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension - Two Hands
why: As above; two hands make it steadier, not lighter on the shoulder.

name: Glute Kickback
why: Quadruped position; the low back arches if the range is chased.

name: Incline Close-Grip Push-Up
why: Elevated hands reduce both the load and the wrist angle.

name: Standing Dumbbell Triceps Extension
why: Overhead position stretches the long head and loads the shoulder to hold it there.

name: Tricep Dumbbell Kickback
why: Short lever, light load, elbow working in mid-range.

name: Triceps Overhead Extension with Rope
why: Overhead under constant cable tension.

name: Upright Row
why: Internal rotation with the arm abducted — the classic impingement position.

name: Air Bike
why: Self-limiting and non-impact, but the effort ceiling is as high as anything here.

name: Battle Ropes
why: Sustained shoulder work at a cardiovascular intensity.

name: Brisk Walking
why: The most universally available conditioning there is. No restriction in the library excludes it.

name: Burpees
why: Maximal-effort whole-body work combining landing impact with a floor transition.

name: Elliptical Trainer
why: Supported, non-impact, and among the better prenatal options. **Flagged for review** — the merged duplicate said otherwise.

name: HIIT Circuit
why: Sustained high effort with form degrading as the circuit progresses.

name: High Knees
why: Running mechanics in place; landing force through knee and ankle.

name: Inchworm
why: Loaded forward fold into a plank; the wrists carry bodyweight at the far end.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
why: Walking mechanics with the incline raising the effort rather than the impact.

name: Jump Rope
why: Repetitive landing impact at high frequency.

name: Jumping Jacks
why: Repeated bilateral landing with the arms overhead.

name: Mountain Climbers
why: Plank position held under a cardiovascular load; shoulders support throughout.

name: Sprint Intervals (HIIT)
why: Near-maximal cardiovascular effort with running impact.

name: Stair Climbing
why: Repeated single-leg knee extension under bodyweight.

name: Stationary Cycling
why: Non-impact and fully supported; resistance is chosen.

name: Swimming
why: Non-weight-bearing. Survives essentially every musculoskeletal restriction.

name: Wrist Circles
why: Unloaded joint preparation.
